about: libcvc's C++ twin of CoPH-Stagewise (NAV-COPH-ROADMAP.md §3.4, §5), written by GRL-SNAM's grl_snam.tools.coph_golden. Doubles are raw bits: 16 hex digits of the uint64, most significant first. Cases: G1 (config), G2 (plant), G3 (potential), G4 (stages), G11 (allocation); in learner, G5 (field fit), G6 (damping fit), G7 (replay) and G8 (update); in packets, G9 (exports, bytes) and G10 (assimilate); episode, G12 (two agents, communication on). G1 and G4 are BIT; G2, G3 and G11 are FLOAT64; in G5-G10 and G12 every value under an 'out' key is FLOAT64 at the section's tier and everything else is BIT.
stage_rules:
The script: tick 0 is observed without a transition. Each later tick observes, then advances.
- Its observation: time = tick * dt; the readings at their script uids, which the learner stores
  as '<agent_id>:<uid>'; the visible obstacles; a footprint (state.x, state.y, sensor_radius,
  time).
- Its transition: Transition(uid = tick - 1, time, x = state[tick - 1], u = (0, 0),
  after = state[tick], version = version[tick - 1]); the learner's version is version[tick]
  before it observes.
observe(observation, transition), on each kept stage s, in order:
1. footprints: the footprint is appended to every s that intersects (x, y, sensor_radius), then
   each list keeps its last footprint_cap.
2. readings: s appends each reading whose uid s does not hold and that s.contains, in order, then
   keeps its last sample_cap.
3. transitions: the newest stage appends the transition, then keeps its last transition_cap.
4. obstacles: s.obstacles = the geometry store's obstacles (ticks[].geometry, in order) that
   intersect s. The store comes from the navigation layer; G4 records it per tick.
advance(x), from the newest stage s:
- delta = |x[:2] - s.center|, size = (stage_width, stage_height). No advance unless
  delta[k] > (size[k] * (1 - overlap)) / 2 for some k.
- axis = argmax(delta / size) (x on a tie); the new centre is s.center with
  center[axis] += sign(x[axis] - center[axis]) * (size[axis] * (1 - overlap)).
- The new stage: id s.id + 1; entry x; target (min(goal.x, (center.x + stage_width / 2) - 0.1),
  goal.y); RBF centres [(cx, cy) for cx in xs for cy in ys], xs = numpy.linspace(center.x -
  stage_width / 2, center.x + stage_width / 2, rbf_side) (i * step + start, the last exactly
  stop), ys likewise with stage_height; weights all -1 / rbf_side^2; version = the learner's.
- Its readings: every kept stage's readings, oldest stage first, that it contains; a repeated uid
  keeps its first place; then the last sample_cap. Its footprints: every kept stage's
  footprints, oldest first, repeats dropped, then the last footprint_cap. No transitions.
- The ring keeps the last previous + 1 stages, and the obstacles are recomputed as in observe.
The tests:
- contains(q): |q.x - center.x| <= stage_width / 2 + 1e-10 and
  |q.y - center.y| <= stage_height / 2 + 1e-10.
- intersects(shape, center): d = max(|shape.xy - center| - (stage_width / 2, stage_height / 2),
  0); d.d <= (reach + 0.12 + safety_margin)^2 + 1e-12. reach is r for a disk (x, y, r) and
  r + hypot(hx, hy) for a slab (x, y, r, hx, hy).
The layout:
- script[tick] = {state: [x, y, vx, vy], version, visible: obstacle indices, readings:
  [[x, y], ...]}. Reading j of a tick has uid '<tick>:<j>' (validation when j % 5 == 0) and
  value (0.05 + 0.01 * j) + 0.001 * (tick % 7), which no ledger rule reads.
- variants[].ticks[tick] = {advanced: null or {id, axis, from_id}, geometry: the store, stages:
  one [id, readings, transitions, footprints, obstacles] per kept stage, oldest first}.
- Readings, transitions and footprints are given against the same stage's lists at the end of
  the previous tick (empty for a new stage) as [dropped, added]: drop that many from the front,
  then append added, written as [start, count] runs of indices. A reading's index counts the
  script's readings in order (5 * tick + j), a transition's is its uid (tick - 1) and a
  footprint's is its tick. Obstacles are indices into obstacles, in the stage's order.
- variants[].created lists each stage's fixed fields when it is made (the first at tick 0).
potential_rules:
model.potential, model.risk, model.shaping_parameters and model.command (no local residual: the
demos never set Stage.local_residual). A case evaluates at q, with velocity v, target t, policy
(pi0, pi1), its scene's RBF centres c_k, weights w_k and obstacles, and rbf_width.
- softplus(z) = log1p(exp(z)), and z itself for z > 20 (torch's threshold); its derivative is
  sigmoid(z), and 1 for z > 20.
- risk(q) = softplus(sum_k w_k exp(-0.5 |(q - c_k) / rbf_width|^2)) / 4.
- An obstacle's clearance is its surface distance minus 0.12 (the agent's radius). A disk
  (x, y, r): |q - (x, y)| - r. A slab (x, y, r, hx, hy), with ends p = (x - hx, y - hy) and
  e = (x + hx, y + hy), d = e - p: |q - (p + clamp(((q - p) . d) / (d . d), 0, 1) d)| - r.
- barrier(q) = sum over obstacles of softplus(6 (0.35 - clearance))^2 / 36 (0 with none).
- shaping(q) = pi0 risk(q) + pi1 barrier(q); s = |q - t|^2.
- legacy (mode 'legacy'): V = 0.5 s + shaping.
- progress (mode 'progress'): V = 0.5 k s + ((alpha s) / (s + ell^2)) shaping, with k, ell, eta
  from shaping and alpha = min(1, 2 eta k ell / bound) (1 when bound = 0), bound =
  policy_bounds[1] (exp(-0.5) sum_k |w_k| / (4 rbf_width) + sum over obstacles of
  softplus(6 (r + 0.47)) / 3). alpha and bound do not depend on q or the policy.
- grad = dV/dq. command: proposed = -grad - 1.4 v; applied = proposed min(1, limit /
  max(|proposed|, 1e-12)).
The layout: potential.scenes[] = {name, center, centers (x0, y0, x1, y1, ...; x outer, as G4's),
weights, obstacles, policy_bounds}; potential.cases[] = {name, scene (an index), mode, q, v,
target, policy, out: {risk, potential, grad, proposed, applied; progress adds alpha, bound}}.
Every point is given under both modes. No point sits at a slab's segment ends or core, or a
disk's centre, where V is not smooth.
allocation_rules:
grl_snam.coph.allocation.allocate (NAV-COPH-ROADMAP §3.3.2), for a force u, a heading psi (rad),
a signed speed v along it, a wheelbase L, a steer lock steer_max, an acceleration limit
accel_max and a speed floor:
- h = (cos psi, sin psi); n = (-sin psi, cos psi), the left normal.
- accel = clamp(u . h, -accel_max, accel_max), with u . h = u.x h.x + u.y h.y.
- kappa = (u . n) / max(v v, speed_floor speed_floor).
- steer = clamp(atan(L kappa), -steer_max, steer_max): the bicycle angle, + left.
- lateral = ((v v) tan(steer)) / L; used = accel h + lateral n; unallocated = u - used.
The layout: allocation.cases[] = {name, u, heading, speed, wheelbase, steer_max, accel_max,
speed_floor, out: {accel, steer, kappa, used, unallocated}}.
learner_rules:
G5-G8 pin CrossingLearner.update, the demos' learner (MazeLearner on TerrainLearner on
CooperativeLearner on Learner), under the profile (stages: the demos' rule, as in G4), at three
snapshots of a scripted crossing run. The C++ reads each snapshot's inputs and reproduces the four
outputs; grl_snam.tools.coph_golden_learner.rebuild is the reference for turning the inputs into a
learner.

The run (inputs; the same bytes on every OS):
- world: one agent, id '0', goal (12, 4), on the crossing's corridor network (nodes, edges) with
  its two doors (obstacles: slabs (x, y, r, hx, hy)); the world's damping 0.85.
- script[tick] = {state: (x, y, vx, vy) at the tick, u: the force held to the next tick, version:
  the learner's version after the tick, readings: 21 (x, y, value) from the demos' sensor lattice
  around state, visible: obstacle indices}. The state follows the exact flow at the world's
  damping; the force is a fixed tracker of a carrot moving east along the middle row to x = 8.6 and
  back. The readings are a rational risk bump at (5, 4.45).
- Each tick: the learner observes (tick 0 without a transition), advances, and updates when
  tick % update_every == 0. A reading's uid is '0:<tick>:<j>' (validation when j % 5 == 0) and its
  time tick * dt. Transition k is (uid k, time (k + 1) * dt, x = state[k], u = u[k], after =
  state[k + 1], version = version[k]). The footprint of tick k is (state[k].x, state[k].y,
  sensor_radius, k * dt).
- After each update the script rounds the committed field weights, damping and policy, and the
  value and gradient of each terrain anchor, to the nearest multiple of 2^-24.

A snapshot (snapshots[]) is the learner's state just before the update at its tick:
- version, damping, policy, now and x (the state passed to update);
- geometry: the geometry store, obstacle indices in the store's order; reported_geometry: the
  navigation context's reported shapes; terrain_anchors: its (x, y, value, gx, gy) anchors in order;
- stages[], oldest first: id, center, entry, target, version, the committed weights; readings and
  transitions and footprints as [start, count] runs of indices (a reading's index is 21 tick + j, a
  transition's its uid, a footprint's its tick), in the stage's own order; obstacles.
- Every stage's entry context, and the navigation context, hold the crossing's network
  (nodes, edges) and maze_graph = true. update adds terrain_anchors and reported_geometry to each
  entry context before it plans (MazeLearner.update, TerrainLearner.update). The demos never set
  Stage.anchors or a local residual, and nothing is received.

G5, field_fit[] (FLOAT64, tier): Learner._field_fit. For each kept stage k, the rows are its
readings with j % 5 != 0, in order: features phi_m(q) = exp(-0.5 |(q - c_m) / rbf_width|^2) over
the stage's 16 RBF centres (new_stage's), target log(expm1(4 max(value, 0.001))). The system is
block diagonal (no continuity rows in the profile): normal_k = A_k^T A_k + fit_ridge I, rhs_k =
A_k^T y_k + fit_ridge w_k (w_k the committed weights); weights_k = normal_k^-1 rhs_k (the Python
solves the stacked system by LU; any solver is within the tier), covariance_k = normal_k^-1.
out per stage: targets, normal (16 x 16, row-major), rhs, weights, covariance.

G6, damping_fit[] (FLOAT64): Learner._fit_damping, then update's reconciliation.
- The records are every kept stage's transitions with uid % 5 != 0 (oldest stage first); with
  fewer than 3, the result is the committed damping and there are no iterates.
- loss(d) = mean over records and the 4 components of (flow(x, u, d, dt) - after)^2
  + 0.05 mean over records of (delta - dt power)^2, with delta = (|v1|^2 - |v0|^2) / 2 and
  power = u . (v0 + v1) / 2 - d (|v0|^2 + |v1|^2) / 2, v0 = x's and v1 = after's velocity
  (flow as in G2).
- From d = the committed damping, solver_steps times: g = loss'(d), h = loss''(d),
  step = d - g / (|h| + 1e-5), next = clamp(step, 0.05, 3). result = the last next.
- proposal = clamp(result, max(damping_bounds[0], damping - damping_trust),
  min(damping_bounds[1], damping + damping_trust)).
out: iterates [{damping, loss, gradient, curvature, step, next}], result, proposal.

G7, replay[] (decisions BIT; values FLOAT64): stage_prediction.retained_replay on the fitted
weights (G5) and the proposal (G6), from the learner as replay_budget.prepare leaves it inside
update (with replay_external_reserve 12).
- plan: prepare's record per stage: eligible, horizon, reason, pilot_steps and the pilots'
  stage handoffs [step, from, to]. budget: the reserve, whether the baseline batch fits, and the
  pilots' steps.
- policies[]: the snapshot's policy, then (0, 0), (10, 10), (0.25, 6), (6, 0.25) and (3, 3).
  Each replays every kept stage from its entry, with a copy of its entry context, for the plan's
  horizon: per step the stage handoff (FrozenStages.advance in the 'spatial' stage mode), the
  routed control (navigation.guarded_control: maze_learning.maze_route on the network, then
  navigation.project with fast = true and the guard, which with maze_graph checks the corridor
  with maze_geometry.corridor_clear), the flow, the support check, then cost += dt (1 + 4 r(after)
  + 0.03 |u|^2) with r the active stage's risk (G3), 40 more on a swept collision, and a stop on
  a collision or within 0.25 of the goal. cost is the mean over the stages that replayed;
  gradient = d cost / d policy. A DomainExit ends the whole batch with no cost (replayed false).
- Decisions: replayed, eligibility [stage, eligible, reason], events [entry, step, from, to],
  controls [entry, step, reason, route_reason, guard_steps, projection_candidates, route_nodes],
  lengths [stage, states], steps (counterfactual steps, guard steps included).
  out: cost, gradient, paths (each replayed stage's states), applied (each control's force),
  waypoints, jumps (each event's shaping jump).
- The replay does not check the budget; update's Learner.replay does, before each batch.

G8, update[] (decisions BIT): Learner.update after G5-G7.
- field validation = mean over every kept stage's readings with j % 5 == 0 of
  (r(q) - value)^2, before with the committed weights and after with G5's; plant validation =
  G6's loss on the records with uid % 5 == 0, before at the committed damping and after at the
  proposal (0 with no records).
- The policy step: the baseline is the replay at the committed policy; the gradient there;
  unconstrained = policy - 0.2 gradient; bounded = clamp to [max(policy_bounds[0], policy -
  policy_trust), min(policy_bounds[1], policy + policy_trust)] per component. Attempt power
  0, 1, ... (up to solver_steps, while the budget holds a batch): candidate = policy + (bounded -
  policy) 0.5^power, accepted when it replays with cost <= baseline + 1e-10; the first accepted
  candidate becomes the policy.
- valid = field after <= field before + validation_slack and plant after <= plant before +
  validation_slack; feasible = proposal within damping_bounds and the policy within [0,
  policy_bounds[1]]; accepted = finite and feasible and valid, else reason
  'validation_or_feasibility'.
- On accept: version + 1, every kept stage takes G5's weights (and covariance) and the new version,
  the damping the proposal and the policy the step's. On reject nothing changes (rollback).
  shaping_jump = V(x) after - V(x) before on the newest stage (G3's progress potential, target the
  goal, the geometry store's obstacles).
- Decisions: field_valid, plant_valid, damping_feasible, policy_in_box, attempts [power, reason,
  accepted], exhausted, independent (the replay did not depend on the policy), accepted, reason,
  version_after. out: field_validation [before, after], plant_validation, margins (before + slack
  - after, each at least 1e-5 away from 0), replay_before, gradient, unconstrained, bounded,
  candidates, costs, policy_after, damping_after, shaping_jump.
packet_rules:
G9 and G10 pin the demos' packets: CrossingLearner.export and .assimilate (MazeLearner on
TerrainLearner on CooperativeLearner), at the snapshots of G5-G8 (learner.snapshots; rebuilt as
learner_rules says). The communication config is learner.world.communication (the profile's,
with ttl 300 and byte_budget 4e6). Recipient and receiver are agent '1'.

A packet (CooperativeLearner's Packet, then MazePacket's two fields) has, in this order: schema,
sender, recipient, identity, timestamp, expires, version, convention, q, p, v, H, V_task, goal,
bounds, anchors, covariance, sources, stage, support_points, uncertainty, acknowledged_sources,
geometry_schema, geometry. In the file: doubles are bits; sources = sorted strings
'<agent>:<tick>:<j>' for the reading indices i (tick, j = divmod(i, 21)), then extra in order;
support_points = the positions of those script readings, in order; a geometry entry is [obstacle
index, sensor (x, y), sensor radius, time, source] for the tuple (*shape, x, y, radius, time,
source), a slab's shape being (x, y, r, hx, hy).

bytes() = the length of json.dumps(asdict(packet), sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'),
allow_nan=False): keys sorted by code point (H and V_task first), tuples as arrays, strings with
JSON's escapes, ints as ints, and every double as Python's repr. repr writes the shortest digits
that read back as the double (the closest such string when two have that length), fixed when the
decimal exponent e of its first digit is -4 <= e < 16 (with '.0' when it is whole), else
d.ddde+XX / d.ddde-XX with at least two exponent digits ('1e-05', '1e+16'); -0.0 keeps its sign.
repr[] lists doubles and their repr; json is export 0's wire packet in full.

G9, exports[] (snapshot k's learner exports to '1' at x = learner.script[tick].state):
- CooperativeLearner.export: the readings are the newest stage's with j % 5 != 0, in order; they
  are grouped into blocks by int(time / (dt update_every)), in order of first appearance (blocks:
  [key, count]). fit(rs) solves (A^T A + fit_ridge I) w = A^T y + fit_ridge w0, A the RBF
  features (G5's) of rs, y = log(expm1(4 clip(value, 0.001, 20))), w0 = -1/16 each. mean =
  fit(all). The ensemble: for each of ensemble_size members, draws[0][member] are block indices
  (with replacement, as many as there are blocks); the member is fit(the readings of those blocks,
  concatenated in draw order). In the demos the indices come from numpy's default_rng seeded with
  seeds[0] (the first 8 hex digits of sha256('<agent>:<repr(now)>:<stage id>')); here they are
  injected, and the C++ draws its own from libcvc's RNG in production.
  candidates: x + (0, 0), (0.4, 0), (0, 0.4), (0, -0.4), each with whether the stage supports it
  (inside its box, and within 0.65 of a fitting reading); the first `anchors` supported are the
  points. field_vector(w, points) = for each point, (r(q), dr/dq) with r G3's risk
  (softplus(phi(q) . w) / 4). anchors = (q, field_vector(mean, q)); covariance = covariance_scale
  (cov(ensemble vectors) + covariance_floor I), cov numpy's (rows are members, n - 1 = 7).
- TerrainLearner.export then replaces anchors and covariance when it can (path 'terrain'): a second
  bootstrap with draws[1] (seed 12345 + int(1000 now)); the readings in order of (-value, uid),
  each kept when the stage supports it and it is more than 0.3 from every point kept so far, until
  `anchors` (picked: their script reading indices); anchors at them from the same mean, and
  covariance = cov(the second ensemble's vectors) + covariance_floor I (no scale). With none
  picked, CooperativeLearner's stay (path 'cooperative').
- The rest: identity '<agent>:<now, 9 decimals>:<stage id>', timestamp now, expires now + ttl,
  version, the convention string, q = x[:2], p = v = x[2:], H = |v|^2 / 2 + G3's potential at q
  (target: the navigation target, else the goal; mean's weights; the policy; the geometry store's
  obstacles), V_task = |q - target|^2 / 2, goal, bounds = the newest stage's box (x0, x1, y0, y1),
  sources = the sorted uids of the readings, stage = its id, support_points = the readings'
  positions, first occurrences in order, uncertainty 'block_bootstrap; calibration_scale=' +
  repr(covariance_scale), no acknowledged sources; geometry_schema 1 and geometry = the learner's
  local geometry reports (geometry: its inputs, in insertion order).
- packet is the wire packet: the export with each anchor's value and gradient, the covariance, H
  and V_task rounded to the nearest multiple of 2^-24. bytes = its bytes() (BIT).
  out (FLOAT64, tier): mean; cooperative {ensemble weights, anchors' (value, gx, gy), covariance};
  terrain {the same} or null; H and V_task (unrounded).

G10, assimilate (the receiver is learner.snapshots[2]'s learner as agent '1': its readings' uids
start '1:', its local geometry reports are receiver.geometry, nothing is received). cases[] are
assimilated in order (MazeLearner.assimilate, then TerrainLearner's, then CooperativeLearner's);
reason, scope and the received senders after each are BIT.
- MazeLearner: geometry_schema must be 1 (else incompatible_geometry). The geometry is valid when
  it has at most 32 entries and each has 8 or 10 values, all finite but the source, radius > 0,
  sensor radius > 0, 0 <= time <= timestamp + 1e-9, source starting '<sender>:geometry:', and the
  sensor within radius + 1e-9 of the shape (slab: slab_distance; disk: |c - sensor| - r); else
  invalid_geometry.
- CooperativeLearner, the first that fails: schema 1 and the convention (incompatible_convention);
  the sender is not the receiver and no source starts '<receiver>:' (returned_evidence); recipient
  (wrong_recipient); sources non-empty, each starting '<sender>:' (invalid_provenance); timestamp
  and expires finite, timestamp <= now + 1e-9, expires >= now, expires >= timestamp (invalid_age);
  (timestamp, stage) > the sender's last accepted pair (duplicate_or_reordered); then
  invalid_payload unless every value is finite, 1 <= #anchors <= `anchors`, covariance is
  3#anchors square, numpy-allclose to its transpose and positive definite, q, p and v have 2
  values, p allclose to v, every anchor value >= 0 and #support_points <= sample_cap; every anchor
  inside bounds (invalid_support); some anchor inside a kept stage's box (unsupported). Eligible:
  received[sender] = packet (an existing sender keeps its place), last[sender] = (timestamp,
  stage), and while more than received_cap are held the oldest timestamp goes (the first such).
- TerrainLearner, for eligible or unsupported: route support is valid when there are support
  points and every anchor is within 0.65 of one; the key is (sender, stage). Invalid support, or a
  held packet at the key with timestamp >= this one, undoes CooperativeLearner's changes (reason
  invalid_remote_support or duplicate_or_reordered). Else remote_terrain[key] = packet, and for each
  anchor the cell (sender, round_half_even(x / 0.2), round_half_even(y / 0.2)) = (expires, anchor,
  identity, sources), the oldest-expiring cells dropped past 128 and the oldest packets past 8;
  last[sender] = (timestamp, stage); reason eligible with scope retained_and_remote_route (or
  remote_route_only when CooperativeLearner said unsupported). The navigation context's
  terrain_anchors become the unexpired cells' anchors (in order) then the learner's own.
- MazeLearner, when eligible: each entry's shape gets a remote report (expires, packet identity,
  source, observation time, sender); reported_geometry = the sorted union of local and remote
  shapes; the shapes that intersect a kept stage join the geometry store (sorted, capped).
- state: what is held afterwards (remote_cells: [sender, ix, iy, expires, anchor, identity];
  terrain_anchors: how many).
- field_fit[], after 'latest' and after the last case (FLOAT64): CooperativeLearner._field_fit. G5's
  fit gives w_k and covariance_k per stage; for each received packet (in order) the anchors inside
  stage k's box (messages: [sender, anchor indices]) give the residual z - f(w_k), f(w) = (value,
  gx, gy) per anchor as field_vector, z the packet's; J = df/dw (analytic: value' = sigmoid(raw) /
  4 phi; gradient' = sigmoid(raw) (1 - sigmoid(raw)) / 4 phi (sum_m dphi_m w_m) + sigmoid(raw) / 4
  dphi, dphi_m = -(q - c_m) / rbf_width^2 phi_m); C = the packet's covariance on those anchors +
  (0.01 + 0.005 (now - timestamp)) I; L = chol(C); rows L^-1 J, targets L^-1 residual, stacked over
  packets. gram = A^T A, rhs = A^T y, delta = (covariance_k^-1 + gram)^-1 rhs, weights = w_k +
  clamp(delta, -0.5, 0.5); a stage with no anchors keeps w_k. rows: the residual's length.
  out: gram, rhs, delta, weights.
- update: the receiver's update at learner.script[112].state, as G8 (decisions BIT) with the
  messages it holds (messages: their identities), each stage's eligibility and plan [stage,
  eligible, horizon, reason, pilot_steps] and the counterfactual steps; out adds each kept stage's
  weights after the update.
episode_rules:
G12 pins the demos' runner (staggered_demo.execute, arm reciprocal_fixed) with two
CrossingLearner agents (MazeLearner on TerrainLearner on CooperativeLearner on Learner) for 60
ticks of the crossing: agent 0 from (0, 4) to (12, 4), agent 1 from (12, 4) to (0, 4), the
crossing's network, its middle door at x = 9.5 and its north door at x = 2.5 (world.obstacles,
slabs), damping 0.85, the profile with steps 60, and CommunicationConfig(byte_budget=4e6, ttl=300).

The world (CrossingWorld): the plant is the exact flow at the world's damping (G2), a step hits when
the motion comes within 0.12 of a door (shapes.slab_sweep) or leaves the corridors
(maze_geometry.corridor_clear, margin 0.12). Sensing at tick t for agent i (world seed
2 seed + i): the 21 lattice points x + sensor_radius (a, b), a, b in linspace(-1, 1, 5),
a^2 + b^2 <= 1, in that order; value_j = max(0.001, 0.02 + noise(i, t, j)), noise = 0.003
(((7 t + 13 j + 5 i) % 11) - 5) / 5; uid '<world seed>:<t>:<j>', which the learner prefixes with
'<agent>:'; the doors within sensor_radius of x (slab_distance) are visible; sensor centre x,
radius sensor_radius. Times are the runner's clock, (120000 t) / 1e6.

The schedule (execute), per boundary t, each agent in turn: complete the held step (the world
steps with the held force, the learner observes with the transition (t - 1, now, x, u, after,
version), the episode ends for it on a hit, within 0.25 of its goal, or at t = 60, else it
advances); at t = 0 it only observes. Then exports: at t % update_every == 0 each active agent
exports to the other (not when either is done). Each packet is delivered to its receiver at the
same boundary (delay 0), in order of (timestamp, identity), and assimilated. Each agent not done
then updates when t % update_every == 0 or it received a packet, and acts (the routed control,
held to the next boundary). The status replies and byte counts never bind at this budget, and the
runner's audits are off.

draws: each sent packet's bootstrap resample indices, [identity, [CooperativeLearner's,
TerrainLearner's]] (G9's draws), recorded from the learner's own generators; the C++ injects them.

Decisions (BIT), per agent: samples [stage, version, done] per boundary; controls per step [tick,
reason, route_reason, route_nodes, waypoint, guard_steps, route_changed]; updates [tick, packets,
accepted, reason, version_after, attempts]; geometry events [kind, obstacle index, source or
packet]; outcome [success, collision]. events: the runner's, in order. out (FLOAT64, atol 1e-6):
per agent the state x at each boundary, the applied force u and the nominal force per step.
